skill.name: auth-handler

content.value_statement: Authentication changes often fail when teams mix session APIs and route guards. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward the project helpers for secure access control.
actual_capabilities: Selects the required wrapper for standard API routes, super admin routes, and cron jobs.
Directs client components to use the project useUser hook for user data.
Directs server code to import auth from the project auth module.
Reminds agents to add per-route protection instead of relying only on middleware.
Points maintainers to project auth files, schema files, and helper locations.
limitations: Does not implement authentication providers or database schema changes by itself.
Assumes the referenced project helpers already exist in the target repository.
Does not validate runtime configuration, secrets, or provider credentials.
Does not replace a full security review of custom authorization logic.

use_cases.title: Protect API Endpoints
use_cases.description: Add the correct authentication wrapper to new or existing API routes.

use_cases.title: Load Current User Data
use_cases.description: Use the approved client or server access pattern for user session data.

use_cases.title: Audit Auth Consistency
use_cases.description: Check whether routes, cron jobs, and admin paths follow the project auth conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Protect a Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API route and apply the correct project authentication wrapper. Keep the existing handler behavior unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Fix User Loading
prompt_templates.scenario: Client or server session access task
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this component or server function for user session access. Replace unsupported session usage with the project-approved pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Secure Admin Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this admin endpoint and ensure it uses the project super admin protection pattern. Explain any authorization assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Auth Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these changed files for route protection, cron authentication, and user data access. List missing safeguards and propose focused fixes.

output_examples.input: A new API route returns account data without an explicit route guard.
output_examples.output: The route should use the standard authenticated wrapper. The existing response logic can stay inside the protected handler.

output_examples.input: A client component reads the session through the unsupported NextAuth hook.
output_examples.output: The component should use the project user hook. This keeps client data access consistent with the application architecture.

output_examples.input: A scheduled endpoint accepts cron requests without the project cron helper.
output_examples.output: The endpoint should use the cron authentication helper. Middleware alone is not enough for this background job path.

best_practices: Protect each sensitive route with the matching project helper, even when middleware already exists.
Use the project user hook in client components and the project auth import on the server.
Check auth provider settings, user schema changes, and required environment values during auth work.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on global middleware for sensitive API routes.
Do not use unsupported session hooks when the project provides its own user hook.
Do not assume minimal session data includes plan or authorization details.

faq.question: What kind of project is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for a Next.js application that uses project-specific authentication helpers and NextAuth v5 patterns.

faq.question: Can it create a new auth system?
faq.answer: No. It guides work inside an existing auth architecture and references existing helper files.

faq.question: Which routes does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers standard API routes, super admin routes, and cron endpoints that need explicit protection.

faq.question: Does it support client user data access?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs client components to use the project useUser hook for user data.

faq.question: Does it check secrets or provider credentials?
faq.answer: No. It mentions relevant environment values, but it does not validate live secrets or provider setup.

faq.question: Can Claude Code and Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
